newsitem.title: JAPAN: TOCOM GOLD FUTURES END HIGHER, PLATINUM DOWN.
newsitem.headline: TOCOM GOLD FUTURES END HIGHER, PLATINUM DOWN.

text.p: Tokyo gold futures ended higher on Tuesday, backed by the yen's weaker tone against the dollar and a rise in bullion prices in the New York market on Monday, but trade was lacklustre, traders said.
Platinum group metals (PGMs) ended lower, following the ending of a strike at South Africa's Impala Platinum Holdings Ltd on Monday, they said.
Gold futures ranged from 12 yen to 16 yen per gram higher. Most-active benchmark June was up 15 yen at 1,212 yen.
Spot gold was quoted at $327.50/90 per ounce at 0723 GMT, down from the New York close of $328.20/70 on Monday.

In gold futures, most private investors were sidelined due to the summer holidays and the lack of clear direction in the currency market. A slim chance that spot gold prices will climb sharply also dampened sentiment, the traders said.
"The spot gold market's bearish sentiment remains intact, based on a view that the fall in U.S. stocks will be short-lived," a trading house trader said.
News that the Impala platinum mine strike had ended put downward pressure on the PGM market, although losses were curbed by late short-covering spurred by the yen's retreat, they said.
"The PGM futures market has been undergoing a technical correction after extremely volatile trade last week," one commodity broker said. "The consolidation phase will continue for some time."
The physical PGM market was quiet due to the summer holidays although the palladium market was still tight even after August deliveries from Russia arrived late last week.

Benchmark June palladium was down 10 yen per gram at 699 yen by the close. Benchmark June platinum was off 13 yen at 1,506 yen. Benchmark June silver was up 3.5 yen per 10 grams at 169.8 yen. --Tokyo Commodities Desk, +81-3-3432-7431
